form.name: Form Studio
form.title: Make something you didn’t see coming.
form.intro: Sculpt a creature. Twist a vessel. Build a repeating pavilion. Ten short lessons turn your first experiment into an editable project, using four supplied models and six purpose-built starters.
form.edition: Form object school · 10 lessons · 3 creative paths

lessons.title: Turn a profile into a statement
lessons.outcome: A fluted vessel with your own silhouette.
lessons.challenge: Make two versions: calm and dramatic. Change only the twist.
steps: Move Twist from 0° toward 100° and watch the flutes spiral.
Try a negative angle to reverse the direction. The source mesh stays editable.
Change Taper to narrow or widen the upper part.
Small changes can make the same profile feel completely different.
Toggle Compare original, then return to your edition.
The camera stays in place so you can compare the geometry.
Open it in Form: the mesh and its twist and taper modifiers remain separate.

lessons.title: Bring the sculpture closer
lessons.outcome: A local sculpt edit on the supplied equestrian model.
lessons.challenge: Inflate a small detail, undo it, then repeat at half the strength.
steps: In Sculpt a detail, choose Inflate.
Orbit first to find a clear part of the sculpture. Brush changes appear when you release.
Drag a short stroke on the model’s surface.
Use a small radius for local details. Each stroke is recorded independently.
Choose Undo stroke and compare the surface.
Undo removes the latest recorded stroke; the source mesh remains intact.
Choose Smooth or Inflate and make another short stroke.
The full Form project keeps the stroke settings and sample positions.

lessons.title: Build a rhythm in space
lessons.features: Ribbon pavilion · arrays · spacing · build history
lessons.outcome: A repeating architectural study built from one rib.
lessons.challenge: Make a tight tunnel, then an open pavilion, using the same source.
steps: Every repeat comes from the same arched source mesh.
Change Spacing and orbit to see the rhythm.
Count controls quantity; spacing controls the distance between ribs.
Move Build history back to Source mesh, then up to Modifiers.
The repeated ribs are generated by a modifier. They are not separate hand-built objects.
Return Build history to 3, then download the project.
In Form, revise the array count and spacing to continue exploring.

lessons.title: Make the detail catch the light
lessons.features: Birds in Orbit · Circle of Anarchy · mesh · lighting
lessons.outcome: A presentation image that reveals the depth of a supplied relief.
lessons.challenge: Switch to Circle of Anarchy and match the same lighting mood.
steps: Try Front, then Perspective. Orbit to inspect the relief from the side.
A relief can look flat from the front. A second angle reveals its depth.
Toggle Mesh to reveal the polygon structure.
This view shows the actual lesson mesh, simplified from the supplied source.
Turn Mesh off and move Light direction.
Compare how changing light reveals edges without changing the geometry.
Choose a finish, frame the view and download a PNG.
This image uses the lesson studio’s lighting. Save the .form file as well to keep editing.

lessons.title: Make the landscape move
lessons.outcome: A reversible terrain variation and an exported surface.
lessons.challenge: Find the smallest displacement that creates a visible change.
steps: Move Surface displacement between 0 and 3 mm.
The seeded displacement is repeatable and stays editable as a modifier.
Toggle Compare original, then return to your version.
The prepared terrain contains geometry without the source sky or texture cards.
Move Build history down to 0 and back to 3.
History lets you inspect the base, recorded strokes and modifier result.
Download STL, then keep the editable .form project too.
STL stores triangles; the Form project also stores the editable operations.

lessons.title: Make it your size
steps: Move Width to give the object a different proportion.
A dimension changes the underlying shape; rotating the view does not.
Change Depth to see the extrusion grow.
The sketch is the footprint. Extrusion gives it a third dimension.
Drag the object or use the view buttons to inspect it.
Inspect more than one angle before deciding the shape is finished.

lessons.title: See how it was made
steps: Move Build history from Sketch to Material.
Each stage adds one decision to the previous stage.
A small rounded edge changes how a surface catches light.
Change Width after adding the finish.
A useful model stays editable after its appearance is developed.

lessons.title: Three objects, one workflow
steps: Choose Ring or Enclosure from the starter menu.
Each starter uses its own proportions and a cut-out sketch.
Start with one proportion before changing several things.
Download a PNG of your object.
An image is useful for a presentation; keep the project for editing.

lessons.title: Find the right finish
steps: Hold the camera still so you can judge the material.
Rough surfaces spread reflections; polished surfaces concentrate them.
Lighting helps reveal the shape; it does not change the geometry.

lessons.title: Keep the editable object
steps: The Form file carries the sketch, feature decisions and appearance.
Choose Open saved project and select your downloaded file.
Opening the source checks that your choices survive the handoff.
STL carries triangles. It does not carry the editable feature history or validate manufacturing suitability.

luma.name: Luma Studio
luma.title: Make an image unmistakably yours.
luma.intro: Take a poster apart, paint a mask, reshape the type and export three formats. Your layers stay separate in the Luma project.

lessons.title: Take the poster apart
steps: A layer keeps one part of the image independently editable.
Hide a layer to understand the work it is doing.
Editable text stays text in your .luma project.

lessons.title: Paint where the color goes
steps: White reveals the treatment; transparent areas retain the original.
Drag across the image to reveal the color treatment.
The mask changes visibility without erasing the source artwork.
Keep creative changes reversible while you explore.

lessons.title: Build three different moods
steps: A preset is a useful starting point, not a final answer.
Watch the bright areas as well as the shadows.
Change Contrast and toggle Treatment to compare.
The original artwork remains available underneath.

lessons.title: Make the type part of the image
steps: Replace NIGHT SCHOOL with your own words.
Short headlines leave room for scale and rhythm.
Spacing changes the feeling without changing the words.
Change Text curve or return it to zero for straight text.
Curved type follows a path; the project keeps the text and path editable.

lessons.title: One design, three outputs
steps: The lesson recomposes its layers for the selected canvas.
The set includes poster, square and story versions.
Open it in Luma to continue with independent text, artwork and treatment layers.

stemdeck.name: StemDeck
stemdeck.title: Make your first mix.
stemdeck.intro: Learn with four original recordings, then open your portable session in the current StemDeck Online studio on Sattari.

lessons.title: Make room for the melody
steps: These are separate original recordings, ready to mix.
Make space by reducing another part before adding more level.
Use Compare with start, then return to your mix.
The comparison uses the same recordings and position.

lessons.title: Hear what each part contributes
steps: Audio starts only when you choose to play it.
Isolation helps you identify its role and texture.
Turn solo off, then mute one deck.
Hear how the remaining arrangement changes.

lessons.title: Choose the moment
steps: The waveform shows the actual recording’s amplitude.
Enable Loop for a deck and adjust its end.
The loop repeats a chosen part of the source recording.
Press Play to audition your region.
Choose boundaries by listening as well as looking.

lessons.title: Move between two groups
steps: The grouping matches StemDeck Online: A/C left, B/D right.
Move the crossfader toward each side.
Watch which two decks belong to each side.
The curve controls how quickly each side changes.

lessons.title: Take your session into the studio
steps: This renders the current cue, loop and mix settings.
The recipe is a readable record of your choices.
Download the portable .sattari project, then open it from the Sattari studio’s Tools / Files controls.
Your four source recordings travel inside the project. The full studio adds arrangement, instruments, effects racks and capture.

scenepilot.name: ScenePilot
scenepilot.title: Turn three clips into a story.
scenepilot.intro: Reorder real clips, place a cut in the music and compare transitions. Keep the edit with its sources.

lessons.title: Choose your opening
steps: The same source clips can tell different stories in a different order.
Move a clip left or right in the timeline.
The opening sets the viewer’s expectations.
Move the playhead through the timeline.
Scrub to inspect the cut, then play to feel its rhythm.

lessons.title: Find the cut in the music
steps: Enable the soundtrack and press Play.
Beat markers describe the supplied music, not a rule you must follow.
Try a cut just before or after a musical accent.
Choose the timing that supports your intention.

lessons.title: Make the suggested edit yours
steps: The lesson supplies a starter edit against the soundtrack’s measured beat map.
A proposal becomes a sequence you can continue editing.
The suggestion remains under your control.

lessons.title: Make a transition earn its place
steps: Both previews use the same source frames and timeline position.
A direct cut can be as deliberate as an effect.
Keep the transition short enough to serve the scene.

lessons.title: Keep the edit and the film
lessons.features: Editable cut map · sources · browser video
steps: Download the ScenePilot cut map and sources.
Keep the project and the source media together for relinking.
Choose Export video and keep this tab visible while it renders.
The lesson offers the recording format your browser supports; Browser Lite’s delivery options are in the full editor.
Play the rendered result in the export preview.
Review the actual exported file before sharing it.
